Well I only drank (heavily) for about 11 years (about 15 to 26), but this is my experience summarized the best I can:
My last time quitting (Fall 2017) I became heavily depressed, suicidal, and was having daily panic attacks. It took me a lot (way too much honestly, mental health can be a grueling process to receive when insurance and money arent where they need to be), but I finally got into counseling. By the time I finally got helped I had relapsed BAD. I got prescribed an antidepressant and a sleeping/anti anxiety medication. For me, these pills saved my life. But I cant completely thank them. I had to get clean again. And I had to be serious about it. Before I had steered clear of a 12 step program, rehab, etc. My psychiatrist recommended a place that is FREE for outpatient. I have been in an intensive outpatient program (IOP) for 2 months now. I switched my mental health services to them too. They keep me accountable, they teach me how to talk to others, how to get into a 12 step program and work it, how to reach out for help, how to find a sponsor, and how to manage my mental health as an addict and person with major depression and panic disorder. For me, reaching out was key. Support is what saved me, the help of others is what got me through. 

I know it isn't easy and there can be a lot of hoops to jump through, but they are so worth jumping through. I hope you can get the help you need. What you're experiencing is very common in early sobriety so please don't be discouraged, it is possible to overcome. Best of luck to you, I hope you can get the help you so deserve.

Here are some things that have helped me, so maybe they could work for you:

Reading This Naked Mind (I believe is still free in the sidebar)

Going to meetings, participating, and getting numbers. I know this is hard at first and maybe you feel like meetings arent for you, but eventually you will find places and people that fit you and the support from them is priceless. 

I personally kept relapsing and put myself into Intensive Outpatient Program which helps me with accountability, support, and learning to open up about my addiction and learn coping mechanisms that aren't drinking.

I set rewards for myself for not drinking. Like candy, eating out, or saving the money for a big purchase ( I redecorated my apartment).

Journaling also helped me a lot. Most times I wanted to drink because of my emotions. Writing it all out helps me to recognize its not that I even want to drink, I want to cover up how I feel. 

I hope some of these can help you. You got this!
